a11s.feedback.p: Open an issue on GitHub (link in the footer of every page) and we will fix it - accessibility defects are treated as the highest priority.
a11s.l1: The help form and remote-assist code are demonstrations - no data is sent anywhere.
a11s.l2: Fonts render differently across operating systems (we load no web fonts, so the site works fully offline).
a11s.l3: Tutorial images are teaching illustrations, not real app screenshots.
a11s.l4: The offline scam-domain list covers international domains only - absence from the list never means "safe".
a11s.m1: Minimum 18px text with fluid scaling; a reading aid offers two larger presets.
a11s.m2: Colour contrast at or above 4.5:1 in both the light and the dark palette. Lighthouse accessibility is gated at 0.95 or better in CI, which fails the build below that.
a11s.m3: Full keyboard support: skip link, visible focus rings, Enter/Space accordions, Escape-closable menu with focus return.
a11s.m4: Respects prefers-reduced-motion, prefers-color-scheme (dark mode) and forced-colors (high contrast).
a11s.m5: Every interactive element carries an accessible name in both languages.
a11s.m6: Keyboard focus is never hidden behind the sticky header (WCAG 2.4.11 focus-not-obscured): jump links land below the bar.
a11s.p1: FilialConnect is built for older adults and people with low digital experience. We target WCAG 2.2 AA across the site and test every change against it.

call.status.p: This site only opens the dialer on your own phone; it cannot send anything by itself. Press call there to reach your family. If nobody answers and this is an emergency, call 120.

call.step2.p: Your own phone app opens with the number already typed in. Nothing leaves your phone until you press call.

card.call.p: One big button opens your phone dialer and calls your family. You can also write a text message yourself.
card.fraud.p: Stay safe from common scams targeting seniors. Learn to recognize phone fraud, fake bank calls, and online deception tactics.
card.guides.p: Download and print clear instructions to take to the bank, hospital, or anywhere. Large print, simple steps, always ready.
card.remote.p: Your children can view your screen remotely and guide you through any app. Secure, private, and family-only access.
card.tutorials.p: Step-by-step guides with large-print steps and simple diagrams for hospital apps, train tickets, banking, and more. No videos needed — just clear text and pictures.

family.p: Type a family member name and phone number once, on the device you use. This site has no server: nothing is uploaded, and no message leaves your phone until you press send in your own phone app.

form.subject: I need help
fraud.1.do1: Hang up immediately—real officials never demand money over the phone
fraud.1.do2: Verify by calling the official number of the agency they claim to represent
fraud.1.do3: Tell your family about the call
fraud.1.how.p: Scammers call pretending to be police, bank staff, or government officials. They claim your bank account is involved in a crime or you owe money, and demand immediate payment.
fraud.1.sign1: Caller claims to be from police, court, or tax bureau
fraud.1.sign2: They ask you to transfer money to a "safe account"
fraud.1.sign3: They threaten arrest or legal action if you do not cooperate
fraud.1.sign4: They tell you not to inform your family
fraud.1.title: Impersonating Police or Officials
fraud.2.do1: Only invest through licensed banks and financial institutions
fraud.2.do2: Consult your children before making any investment decisions
fraud.2.do3: Remember: if it sounds too good to be true, it is
fraud.2.how.p: Scammers invite you to WeChat or QQ groups promising high returns on gold, stocks, cryptocurrency, or health products. They show fake profits to convince you to invest more, then disappear with your money.
fraud.2.sign2: Pressure to invest quickly before the "opportunity disappears"
fraud.2.sign3: Group chat where everyone seems to be making money
fraud.2.sign4: Asked to download unknown apps for investment
fraud.2.title: Fake Investment Schemes
fraud.3.do1: Never install software at a stranger's request
fraud.3.do2: Hang up—real tech companies do not make unsolicited calls
fraud.3.do3: If concerned, ask a family member to check your device
fraud.3.how.p: Someone calls claiming your computer or phone has a virus. They ask you to install software that lets them control your device remotely, then steal your banking information.
fraud.3.sign1: Unsolicited call about problems with your computer or phone
fraud.3.sign2: Asked to install remote access software
fraud.3.title: Fake Customer Service Scams
fraud.4.do1: Real prizes never require you to pay first
fraud.4.do2: Delete the message and block the sender
fraud.4.do3: Never share your banking information with strangers
fraud.4.how.p: You receive a message or call saying you have won a prize, lottery, or sweepstakes. To claim it, you need to pay a "processing fee" or "tax" first. The prize never arrives.
fraud.4.sign1: You "won" a contest you never entered
fraud.4.sign2: You must pay money before receiving the prize
fraud.4.sign3: Urgent deadline to claim the prize
fraud.4.sign4: Asked for bank details to "deposit" the prize
fraud.4.title: Prize and Lottery Scams
fraud.5.do1: Never click links in unexpected messages
fraud.5.do2: If "family" asks for money, call them first to verify
fraud.5.do3: Type website addresses yourself instead of clicking links
fraud.5.how.p: You receive a text or WeChat message with a link that looks like it is from your bank, delivery company, or family. Clicking it takes you to a fake website that steals your login and password.
fraud.5.sign1: Message with a link you were not expecting
fraud.5.sign2: Link looks slightly wrong (extra letters, misspellings)
fraud.5.sign3: Urgent message like "Your account will be closed"
fraud.5.sign4: Message from "family" asking for money through a new number
fraud.5.title: Phishing Link Scams
fraud.banner.p: Banks, police, and government agencies will NEVER call to ask for your password, verification code, or to transfer money. If someone does, hang up immediately.
fraud.p: Knowledge is your best defense. Learn to recognize scams before they find you.
fraud.report.p: If you think you have encountered a scam, tell your family immediately. They can help you verify and report it.

guides.p: Download and print step-by-step instructions. Take them to the bank, hospital, or anywhere you need. Large print, simple steps, always ready.
hero.p: Bridging the digital divide for seniors. One click connects them to the help they need, when they need it most.
linkcheck.bad: Warning: this domain is on the known scam list. Do not click, do not enter any information. Close it and tell your family.
linkcheck.errload: Cannot load the offline list. Open this site through a web server (file:// blocks data loading).
linkcheck.note: Offline list from destroylist (MIT). Your input never leaves this page.
linkcheck.ok: Not found in the scam list. That does NOT mean it is safe. Never enter passwords or verification codes on unfamiliar sites.
linkcheck.p: Paste a link or domain from a text message or stranger. It is checked offline against a list of known scam domains. No internet connection needed.
linkcheck.parse: Cannot recognize a domain here. Paste a full link, or a domain like example.com.
linkcheck.placeholder: Paste a link or domain here
linkcheck.scope: Scope: this offline list holds about 83,000 international phishing domains; fewer than 1% are Chinese (.cn). Phone scams and in-app scripts are not in it, so a clean result does not mean the message is safe.
remote.code.note: Every visit shows a different practice code, so you can point at what you are looking at without sharing anything.
remote.code.p: This is a practice code, not a connection. Real screen sharing happens inside the app you agree on with your family.
remote.codes.h4: The Code Is A Practice Label
remote.codes.p: It is generated in your own browser and never leaves your phone. Do not treat it as a security feature of any real tool.
remote.control.p: When you share your screen in another app, that app decides what the other person can do, and you can stop it there at any time.
remote.cta.p: If you cannot wait, use the Call For Help page: it opens the dialer or a message on your own phone and sends nothing by itself.
remote.demo.h4: Real Screen Sharing Lives In Another App
remote.demo.p: This page is a rehearsal, not a remote-control tool. To let a relative see your phone, open the app you both trust, start its screen share, and stop it when you are done.
remote.family.p: This page has no server and no session. Nobody can join your phone from here, and it does not start any app on your phone.
remote.nodata.p: This site records no visits and no screen content. If you share your screen through another app, that app's own rules apply.
remote.p: Ask your child to guide you through a phone problem: this page gives you the words to say, and shows which screen-sharing features your phone already has. Nothing here connects to anything.
remote.security.h2: What This Page Does Not Do
remote.security.p: Read this before you share your screen with anyone
remote.step1.p: A short code appears on the screen. It is only a label for practising - this site does not connect to anything.
remote.step2.p: Use the Call For Help page, or phone them yourself. Read the code out so you both know which screen you mean.
remote.step3.h4: Share The Screen In That App
remote.step3.p: WeChat on a computer can share your phone screen, and phones have a built-in screen share for support. This site does not do it for you - it only helps you ask for it.
remote.steps.p: Three steps, using a phone feature you already have

tut-detail.banking.img.alt: Illustration: a banking app home with a balance card, three service icons, and a privacy reminder button
tut-detail.banking.p: Manage your money safely using your bank app. Check balances, transfer funds, and pay bills from home.
tut-detail.banking.step1.p: Find your bank app on your phone. Each bank has its own app. If you have trouble, ask your children to help you install it.
tut-detail.banking.step1.title: Open Your Bank App
tut-detail.banking.step2.p: Enter your account number and password. Never share your password with anyone. If you forget it, go to your bank branch to reset it.
tut-detail.banking.step2.title: Log In Safely
tut-detail.banking.step3.p: Tap "My Account" or "Balance" to see how much money you have. The display is clear and easy to read.
tut-detail.banking.step3.title: Check Your Balance
tut-detail.banking.step4.p: Tap "Transfer" to send money to another account. You need the recipient name, bank, and account number. Double-check all details before confirming.
tut-detail.banking.step4.title: Transfer Money
tut-detail.banking.step5.p: Tap "Payments" to pay utility bills, phone bills, and more. The app stores your payment history so you can review it later.
tut-detail.banking.step5.title: Pay Bills
tut-detail.banking.step6.p: Never click links in messages claiming your account has problems. Log in only through the official app. If you receive suspicious calls, hang up and tell your family.
tut-detail.banking.step6.title: Stay Safe
tut-detail.hospital.h1: How to Book a Doctor Appointment
tut-detail.hospital.img.alt: Illustration: a hospital app screen with date chips, department rows, and a large orange appointment button
tut-detail.hospital.p: Follow these simple steps to book a doctor appointment using your phone. No need to wait in long lines at the hospital.
tut-detail.hospital.step1.p: Find the hospital app on your phone. Common apps include health department platforms or your local hospital app. If you do not have one, ask your children to help you install it.
tut-detail.hospital.step1.title: Open the Hospital App
tut-detail.hospital.step2.p: Type the name of your hospital in the search bar. Make sure you select the correct hospital, as some cities have multiple branches.
tut-detail.hospital.step2.title: Search for Your Hospital
tut-detail.hospital.step3.p: Choose the department you need, such as Internal Medicine, Cardiology, or Orthopedics. If you are unsure, ask your family or choose General Internal Medicine.
tut-detail.hospital.step3.title: Select the Department
tut-detail.hospital.step4.p: Browse available doctors and time slots. Pick a date and time that works for you. Morning slots are usually easier to get.
tut-detail.hospital.step4.title: Choose a Doctor and Time
tut-detail.hospital.step5.p: Review your appointment details and pay the registration fee. Most apps accept WeChat Pay or Alipay. The fee is usually small.
tut-detail.hospital.step5.title: Confirm and Pay
tut-detail.hospital.step6.p: After booking, you will receive a confirmation. Check the app for your appointment number and queue position before going to the hospital.
tut-detail.hospital.step6.title: View Your Appointment
tut-detail.hospital.step7.p: Arrive 30 minutes early. Go directly to the department floor and wait for your number to be called. Bring your ID and insurance card.
tut-detail.hospital.step7.title: Arrive at the Hospital
tut-detail.medical.img.alt: Illustration: a test report screen with three result rows, each marked normal with a green check
tut-detail.medical.p: Learn to read your health check results. Know what the numbers mean before your next doctor visit.
tut-detail.medical.related1: How to Book a Doctor Appointment
tut-detail.medical.step1.p: Medical reports can be found in the hospital app, or you may receive a paper copy. Ask the hospital staff if you need help locating it.
tut-detail.medical.step1.title: Find Your Report
tut-detail.medical.step2.p: Most reports start with a summary. Look for any items marked with an arrow up (↑) or down (↓), which means the value is higher or lower than normal.
tut-detail.medical.step2.title: Read the Summary First
tut-detail.medical.step3.p: Fasting blood sugar (glucose) should be between 3.9-6.1 mmol/L. If it is higher, talk to your doctor about diabetes prevention.
tut-detail.medical.step3.title: Check Blood Sugar
tut-detail.medical.step4.p: Normal blood pressure is below 120/80. The first number (systolic) is pressure when your heart beats. The second (diastolic) is pressure between beats.
tut-detail.medical.step4.title: Check Blood Pressure Numbers
tut-detail.medical.step5.p: Total cholesterol should be below 5.2 mmol/L. HDL (good cholesterol) should be high. LDL (bad cholesterol) should be low.
tut-detail.medical.step5.title: Understand Cholesterol
tut-detail.medical.step6.p: Write down any items with abnormal values. Bring this list to your doctor visit so you can ask questions about each one.
tut-detail.medical.step6.title: Note Any Abnormal Items
tut-detail.medical.step7.p: Never self-diagnose based on a report. Always discuss results with your doctor. They can explain what each number means for your specific health situation.
tut-detail.medical.step7.title: Ask Your Doctor
tut-detail.ride.img.alt: Illustration: a ride-hailing map showing a route from a green pickup dot to an orange destination dot
tut-detail.ride.p: Call a taxi from your phone anytime. No need to stand on the street waiting.
tut-detail.ride.step1.p: Find the ride-hailing app on your phone. Common apps include DiDi and other local services. Tap to open.
tut-detail.ride.step1.title: Open the Ride App
tut-detail.ride.step2.p: The app usually detects your current location automatically. If it is wrong, tap the location box and enter your address manually.
tut-detail.ride.step2.title: Set Your Pickup Location
tut-detail.ride.step3.p: Type the address or name of where you want to go. The app will show estimated arrival time and fare.
tut-detail.ride.step3.title: Enter Your Destination
tut-detail.ride.step4.p: Select "Express" for a standard affordable ride, or "Comfort" for a nicer car. Express is usually sufficient for everyday trips.
tut-detail.ride.step4.title: Choose Car Type
tut-detail.ride.step5.p: Tap "Confirm" to request a ride. The app will match you with a driver. You can see the driver name, car type, and license plate number.
tut-detail.ride.step5.title: Confirm and Wait
tut-detail.ride.step6.p: Watch the driver approach on the map. When the car arrives, check the license plate matches. Get in and enjoy your ride.
tut-detail.ride.step6.title: Track Your Ride
tut-detail.ride.step7.p: After arriving, the app asks you to rate the driver. A 5-star rating is the default. Payment is automatic through the app.
tut-detail.ride.step7.title: Rate After the Trip
tut-detail.train.img.alt: Illustration: a ticket booking screen with a route, two train options, and a large orange pay button
tut-detail.train.p: Book train tickets from home using the official 12306 app. No need to go to the station ticket window.
tut-detail.train.step1.p: The official railway app is called 12306. If you do not have it, ask your children to help you install it from the official app store.
tut-detail.train.step1.title: Open the 12306 App
tut-detail.train.step2.p: Enter your departure city and destination city. Select the date you want to travel. The app will show all available trains.
tut-detail.train.step2.title: Search for Your Route
tut-detail.train.step3.p: Compare trains by departure time, duration, and price. High-speed trains (G/D series) are faster. Regular trains (K/T series) are cheaper.
tut-detail.train.step3.title: Choose Your Train
tut-detail.train.step4.p: Choose your seat type: Second Class is affordable, First Class is more comfortable, Business Class is premium. For short trips, Second Class is fine.
tut-detail.train.step4.title: Select Seat Type
tut-detail.train.step5.p: Enter the name and ID number of each passenger. Make sure the information matches your ID card exactly.
tut-detail.train.step5.title: Add Passenger Information
tut-detail.train.step6.p: Pay using WeChat Pay, Alipay, or bank card. After payment, your e-ticket is stored in the app.
tut-detail.train.step6.title: Pay for Your Ticket
tut-detail.train.step7.p: At the station, you can use your ID card directly at the gate for e-ticket entry, or print a paper ticket at the self-service machines.
tut-detail.train.step7.title: Collect Your Ticket or Use E-Ticket
tut-detail.wechat.img.alt: Illustration: a family group chat with message bubbles and a highlighted plus button for video calls
tut-detail.wechat.p: Master the most useful WeChat features step by step. From chatting with family to paying at stores.
tut-detail.wechat.step1.p: Find the WeChat icon on your phone. It is a green icon with two chat bubbles. Tap it to open.
tut-detail.wechat.step1.title: Open WeChat
tut-detail.wechat.step2.p: Tap the "+" button at the top right, then "Add Contacts." You can search by WeChat ID or phone number, or scan a QR code.
tut-detail.wechat.step2.title: Add Contacts
tut-detail.wechat.step3.p: Tap a contact name to open a chat. Type your message and tap Send. You can also send voice messages by holding the microphone button.
tut-detail.wechat.step3.title: Send Messages
tut-detail.wechat.step4.p: In a chat, tap the "+" icon and select "Video Call." This lets you see your family face-to-face, even from far away.
tut-detail.wechat.step4.title: Make Video Calls
tut-detail.wechat.step5.p: Tap "Me" then "Pay" to set up WeChat Pay. You can pay at stores by scanning QR codes, send money to friends, and pay bills.
tut-detail.wechat.step5.title: Use WeChat Pay
tut-detail.wechat.step6.p: In WeChat, tap "Discover" then "Mini Programs." Search for grocery delivery apps. You can order fresh food and daily necessities delivered to your door.
tut-detail.wechat.step6.title: Order Groceries
tut-detail.wechat.step7.p: Do not click unfamiliar links. Do not transfer money to strangers. If someone asks for money through a new number, call your family to verify first.
tut-detail.wechat.step7.title: Stay Safe on WeChat
